why: Peeking means looking one item ahead without consuming it: wrap the iterator and cache the next value, so peek reads the cache and next returns the cache and refills it.
hints: The underlying iterator cannot un-read a value. What could you store so peek does not lose it?
Hold one look-ahead slot. peek returns it; next returns it and loads the following value; hasNext checks whether the slot is filled.
Implement with an index into nums (or a cached value plus a flag). Every operation is O(1).
pitfalls: Repeated peeks must return the same value.
hasNext after the last next is false; return the strings "true"/"false", and numbers as decimal strings.
statement:
You are given an array nums and a list of operations to run, in order, on one iterator over nums:

  • peek: return the next value without moving past it.
  • next: return the next value and move past it.
  • hasNext: return "true" if a value remains, else "false".

Return one string per operation. Every peek and next is guaranteed to have a value available.

Worked example: nums = [1,2,3], operations [peek, next, peek, next, hasNext]

  • peek sees 1, position unchanged: "1"
  • next returns 1 and advances: "1"
  • peek sees 2: "2"
  • next returns 2: "2"
  • hasNext: 3 remains: "true"

Answer: ["1","1","2","2","true"].
